proposals.before: Phagpa, born at age seven, recited scriptures of several hundred thousand words, and could roughly penetrate their great meaning; the people of his country called him the Holy Child, hence he was named Phagpa.
proposals.after: When Phagpa was seven years old, he recited scriptures of several hundred thousand words, and could roughly penetrate their great meaning; the people of his country called him the Holy Child, hence he was named Phagpa.
proposals.reason: 生七歲 marks age seven, not that he was born already aged seven.

proposals.before: Sakya Pandita succeeded him and died in the second year of the Huangqing era.
proposals.after: Xiangjiaban succeeded him and died in the second year of the Huangqing era.
proposals.reason: 相家班 is a Yuan imperial preceptor who died in Huangqing 2 (AD 1313), not the earlier figure known as Sakya Pandita.

proposals.before: Sakya Pandita succeeded; in the second year of Huangqing he died.
proposals.after: Xiangjiaban succeeded; in the second year of Huangqing he died.
proposals.reason: The literal English likewise misidentifies 相家班 as Sakya Pandita despite the Huangqing death date.

proposals.before: Once a tributary state submitted a memorial inscribed in gold lettering. The emperor sent for Vimuktisri while the entire court watched in astonishment to see how he would handle it.
proposals.after: Once a tributary state submitted a memorial inscribed in gold lettering. The emperor sent someone to examine it, while the entire court watched in astonishment to see how it would be handled.
proposals.reason: Chinese 帝遣視之 does not name Vimuktisri as the person sent; the next sentence first names him as the one who then treated the gold leaf.

proposals.before: In the second year of the Zhishun era he received a jade seal and the added title State Preceptor of the Tripitaka, Universal Enlightenment, Perfect Illumination, and Great Eloquence.
proposals.after: In the second year of the Zhishun era he received a jade seal and the added title State Preceptor of the Tripitaka, Universal Enlightenment, Perfect Illumination, Broad Radiance, and Great Eloquence.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits 廣照 (Broad Radiance) from the title 普覺圓明廣照弘辯三藏國師.

proposals.before: During Taiding, because the Imperial Preceptor's younger brother Kun dga' ye shes rgyal mtshan was about to arrive, an edict ordered the Central Secretariat to hold sheep and wine for suburban welcome;
proposals.after: During Taiding, because the Imperial Preceptor's younger brother Kun dga' ye shes was about to arrive, an edict ordered the Central Secretariat to hold sheep and wine for suburban welcome;
proposals.reason: Literal English invents rgyal mtshan; the Chinese names only 公哥亦思監.

proposals.before: One was called Sasinatun, meaning the Great Divine Mantra of the Li Kingdom.
proposals.after: One was called Sasinatun, meaning the Great Divine Mantra of the Dali Kingdom.
proposals.reason: The Chinese gloss is 大理, the Dali kingdom, not a truncated Li Kingdom.

proposals.before: There is one called Sasinatun, which in Chinese means the "Great Divine Mantra of the Li Kingdom."
proposals.after: There is one called Sasinatun, which in Chinese means the "Great Divine Mantra of the Dali Kingdom."
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise misrenders 大理 as Li Kingdom rather than Dali.

proposals.before: In the fourth year of the Yanyou era the Xuanwei Commissioner tallied annual supplies for inner-court Buddhist affairs by weight: four hundred thirty-nine thousand five hundred jin of flour, seventy-nine thousand of oil, twenty-one thousand eight hundred seventy of butter, and twenty-seven thousand three hundred of honey.
proposals.after: In the fourth year of the Yanyou era the Xuanhui Commissioner tallied annual supplies for inner-court Buddhist affairs by weight: four hundred thirty-nine thousand five hundred jin of flour, seventy-nine thousand of oil, twenty-one thousand eight hundred seventy of butter, and twenty-seven thousand three hundred of honey.
proposals.reason: 宣徽使 is the Xuanhui commissioner, not 宣慰 Xuanwei.

proposals.before: In the fourth year of Yanyou, the Xuanwei Commissioner tallied what the inner court Buddhist affairs supplied each year, measured in jin: flour four hundred thirty-nine thousand five hundred, oil seventy-nine thousand, butter twenty-one thousand eight hundred seventy, honey twenty-seven thousand three hundred.
proposals.after: In the fourth year of Yanyou, the Xuanhui Commissioner tallied what the inner court Buddhist affairs supplied each year, measured in jin: flour four hundred thirty-nine thousand five hundred, oil seventy-nine thousand, butter twenty-one thousand eight hundred seventy, honey twenty-seven thousand three hundred.
proposals.reason: Literal English repeats the Xuanwei misreading of 宣徽使.

proposals.before: Thereupon he bestowed on him a tiger tally, with imperial writ as supplement, not reproaching his name but only calling him "Immortal."
proposals.after: Thereupon he bestowed on him a tiger tally, with imperial writ as supplement, not addressing him by his personal name but only calling him "Immortal."
proposals.reason: 不斥其名 means not calling him by his personal name, not 'reproaching' the name.

proposals.before: In dinghai, he again prayed for drought; he set a term of three days' rain as an auspicious response — afterward it was also verified.
proposals.after: In dinghai, he again prayed on account of drought; he set a term of three days' rain as an auspicious response — afterward it was also verified.
proposals.reason: 為旱禱 is prayer because of drought, not prayer for drought.

proposals.before: An Tong was moved by his words; therefore when he served as the Founder's of the Dynasty's chancellor, he took purity, tranquility, and loyalty as his main principles.
proposals.after: An Tong was moved by his words; therefore when he served as chancellor to the Founder of the Dynasty (Shizu), he took purity, tranquility, and loyalty as his main principles.
proposals.reason: Literal English is ungrammatical ('Founder's of the Dynasty's') and 世祖 is Shizu, not the earlier 太祖 Founder.

proposals.before: The Zhengyi Heavenly Master lineage began with Zhang Daoling of the Han dynasty. After four generations the family surname became Sheng, and they settled at Dragon-Tiger Mountain in Xin prefecture.
proposals.after: The Zhengyi Heavenly Master lineage began with Zhang Daoling of the Han dynasty. The fourth generation, Sheng, came to dwell at Dragon-Tiger Mountain in Xin prefecture.
proposals.reason: 四代曰盛 names the fourth-generation master Sheng (張盛), not a change of family surname.

proposals.before: The Zhengyi Heavenly Master began with Zhang Daoling of Han; afterward four generations called Sheng came to dwell at Dragon-Tiger Mountain in Xin.
proposals.after: The Zhengyi Heavenly Master began with Zhang Daoling of Han; afterward the fourth generation, named Sheng, came to dwell at Dragon-Tiger Mountain in Xin.
proposals.reason: 四代曰盛 is the fourth generation named Sheng, not multiple generations called Sheng.

proposals.before: He was promoted to Honorary Three Excellencies of the First Rank and given the added title Great Patriarch of the Xuan Teaching, Assisting Completion and Praising Transformation. A jade seal was carved and bestowed upon him.
proposals.after: He was promoted to Opening the Mansion, Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, and given the added title Great Patriarch of the Xuan Teaching, Assisting Completion, Praising Transformation, and Protecting the Fortune. A jade seal of the Great Patriarch of the Xuan Teaching was carved and bestowed upon him.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic rendering omits 保運 from the honorific title and does not specify that the jade seal was the 玄教大宗師印 named in the Chinese.

proposals.before: The following year he was appointed Special Advancement, Supreme Minister, Great Patriarch of the Xuan Teaching, and Perfected One of Honoring Culture and Expanding the Way, placed in charge of Daoism throughout Jianghuai, Jingxiang, and other regions, and made director of the Hall of Worthies for Daoist affairs, with one jade seal and two silver seals.
proposals.after: The following year he was appointed Special Advancement, Supreme Minister, Great Patriarch of the Xuan Teaching, and Perfected One of Honoring Culture, Expanding the Way, and Mysterious Virtue, placed in charge of Daoism throughout Jianghuai, Jingxiang, and other regions, and made director of the Hall of Worthies for Daoist affairs, with one jade seal and two silver seals.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits 玄德 from the religious title 崇文弘道玄德真人, which the Chinese and literal both include.

proposals.before: The Supreme Unity teaching was founded by the Daoist priest Xiao Baozhen during the Jintianjuan era of the Jin dynasty, who transmitted the arts of the Supreme Unity Three Origins talismans and named the teaching accordingly.
proposals.after: The Supreme Unity teaching was founded by the Daoist priest Xiao Baozhen during the Tianjuan era of the Jin dynasty, who transmitted the arts of the Supreme Unity Three Origins talismans and named the teaching accordingly.
proposals.reason: Jintianjuan fuses the polity 金 with the reign 天眷; the source dates the founding to Tianjuan of Jin.

proposals.before: The Supreme Unity teaching began with the Daoist priest Xiao Baozhen in the Jintianjuan period of Jin, transmitting the arts of the Supreme Unity Three Origins talismans — therefore naming the teaching Supreme Unity.
proposals.after: The Supreme Unity teaching began with the Daoist priest Xiao Baozhen in the Tianjuan period of Jin, transmitting the arts of the Supreme Unity Three Origins talismans — therefore naming the teaching Supreme Unity.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise fuses 金天眷 into Jintianjuan instead of Tianjuan of Jin.

proposals.before: He also spoke through Court Regalia Officer Dong Wenzong. Kublai was pleased and said, "It shall soon be done."
proposals.after: He also spoke through Court Regalia Officer Dong Wenzhong. Kublai was pleased and said, "It shall soon be done."
proposals.reason: 董文忠 is Wenzhong, not Wenzong; the English misspells the given name.

proposals.before: Moreover, through Court Regalia Officer Dong Wenzong he also spoke on this; the Founder of the Dynasty was pleased and said: "It will soon be carried out."
proposals.after: Moreover, through Court Regalia Officer Dong Wenzhong he also spoke on this; the Founder of the Dynasty was pleased and said: "It will soon be carried out."
proposals.reason: Literal English repeats the same 文忠 > Wenzong error.

decisions.reason: 生七歲 means that Phagpa was seven years old, not that he was born already aged seven; the proposed literal restores that age reading without adding or dropping anything else.
The person who 嗣 and died in 皇慶二年 is named 相家班, a later Yuan imperial preceptor, not the thirteenth-century Sakya Pandita.
The literal field repeats the same misidentification of 相家班 as Sakya Pandita; Xiangjiaban matches this successor who died in Huangqing 2.
帝遣視之 does not name the envoy; 必蘭納識理 first appears in the next sentence when he treats the gold leaf, so inserting Vimuktisri here is unsupported.
The idiomatic title skipped 廣照 in 普覺圓明廣照弘辯三藏國師; inserting Broad Radiance restores the omitted epithet without other changes.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 普覺圓明廣照弘辯三藏國師

decisions.reason: The Chinese names only 公哥亦思監; the literal rgyal mtshan is an invented extra name element not present in this unit.

decisions.after: One was called Sasinatun, meaning the Heavenly God Mantra of the Dali Kingdom.
decisions.reason: 華言《大理天神咒》 names the Dali kingdom, not a Li Kingdom, but 大 belongs to 大理 and is not a separate 'Great'; the proposal still keeps that leftover 'Great'.

decisions.after: There is one called Sasinatun, which in Chinese means the "Heavenly God Mantra of the Dali Kingdom."
decisions.reason: The literal likewise misread 大理 as Li Kingdom; replacing Li with Dali while retaining 'Great Divine Mantra' still treats 大 as an extra adjective.
The office is 宣徽使, the Xuanhui commissioner, not 宣慰使; Xuanwei is a different Yuan title.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 宣徽使會每歲內廷佛事所供

decisions.reason: The literal field repeats the Xuanwei misreading of 宣徽使; Xuanhui is the correct transcription of 徽.
不斥其名 is the honorific practice of not using his personal name, matching 惟曰「神仙」, not reproaching a name.
為旱禱 means he prayed because of drought, with rain as the expected response; 'prayed for drought' reverses the purpose.

decisions.after: An Tong was moved by his words; therefore when he served as chancellor to the Founder of the Dynasty, he took purity, tranquility, and loyalty as his main principles.
decisions.reason: The original 'Founder's of the Dynasty's' is ungrammatical for 其相世祖也, but the parenthetical (Shizu) is an added gloss; this chapter's literal already renders 世祖 as Founder of the Dynasty.
四代曰盛 identifies the fourth-generation master named Sheng, who came to dwell at Longhu; it does not say the family surname changed to Sheng.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 其後四代曰盛，來居信之龍虎山

decisions.reason: 四代曰盛 is one fourth-generation figure named Sheng, not several generations all called Sheng.

decisions.after: He was promoted to Honorary Three Excellencies of the First Rank and given the added title Great Patriarch of the Xuan Teaching, Assisting Completion, Praising Transformation, and Protecting the Fortune. A jade seal of the Great Patriarch of the Xuan Teaching was carved and bestowed upon him.
decisions.reason: The original omits 保運 and the named 玄教大宗師印, but rewriting 開府儀同三司 as Opening the Mansion is only a stylistic recast of an already serviceable idiomatic office title.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 加號輔成贊化保運玄教大宗師，刻玉為玄教大宗師印以賜

decisions.reason: 崇文弘道玄德真人 includes 玄德, which the idiomatic title dropped; adding Mysterious Virtue restores the missing epithet.
金天眷中 is the Tianjuan era under Jin; Jintianjuan fuses the dynasty name into the reign title.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 始金天眷中道士蕭抱珍

decisions.reason: The literal likewise fused 金天眷 into Jintianjuan; Tianjuan period of Jin matches the source dating.
董文忠 is Wenzhong; Wenzong would be 文宗 and is a misspelling of this given name.
The literal field repeats Wenzong for 文忠; Wenzhong is the correct reading of the same name.

claimRevisions.reason: The accepted repair shows that the English personal name Sakya Pandita was produced only by the mistranslation of 相家班; the person and Chinese name remain, so the English value is corrected to Xiangjiaban.
